Maintenance Report — MNT-0049-001

Asset: WELL-0049 (SW-23 Well 049, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 23 Oct 2022 08:00 · Finished: 08 Nov 2022 05:00 · Well stopped for this job: 381 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Kevin Price, Brian Coleman · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0049-0001 on 2022-10-20 Report written: 09 Nov 2022

What happened

Field staff reported that oil was dripping from the gearbox onto the pump jack base. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0049-0001 showed the wellhead at 25.8 °C with the air at 23.8 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 14 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

A hardened output shaft seal after years of service.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0049-001 (WS-06).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0049-003

Asset: WELL-0049 (SW-23 Well 049, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 31 Dec 2022 08:00 · Finished: 06 Feb 2023 21:00 · Well stopped for this job: 901 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Brian Coleman, Kevin Price · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0049-0011 on 2022-12-29 Report written: 08 Feb 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0049-0011 showed the wellhead at 15.4 °C with the air at 11.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 36 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

Total6,321

Notes and recommendations

  • Shorten the grease interval on this unit to 60 days.
  • Check saddle bearings on neighbouring units of the same age.

maintenance.action: Replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0049-006

Asset: WELL-0049 (SW-23 Well 049, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 28 Apr 2023 08:00 · Finished: 22 May 2023 23:00 · Well stopped for this job: 591 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Kevin Price · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0049-0028 on 2023-04-27 Report written: 22 May 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the electric motor driving the pump jack had stopped and would not restart. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0049-0028 showed the wellhead at 26.9 °C with the air at 25.2 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 23 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Winding breakdown from heat and age. This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's pump jack in the last 12 months.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

Notes and recommendations

  • Clean the motor cooling fins at each scheduled service.

maintenance.action: Replaced the flange gasket and bolts and remediated soil
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0049-009

Asset: WELL-0049 (SW-23 Well 049, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 29 Sep 2023 08:00 · Finished: 29 Sep 2023 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 10 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0049-0050 on 2023-09-28 Report written: 30 Sep 2023

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0049-0050 at 12:30 on 2023-09-28 found crude oil on the pad: about 1.5% of the pad area, estimated 0.7 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 3.2 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

Root cause

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Cleaned free oil out of the cellar.
  2. Unbolted the flange and removed the failed gasket.
  3. Fitted a new gasket and new bolts, torqued to specification.
  4. Excavated the stained soil around the cellar.

Summary of the fix: replaced the flange gasket and bolts and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 390 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 312 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 0.5 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0049-009 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.7% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Total10,282

Asset: WELL-0049 (SW-23 Well 049, T350, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 15 Feb 2025 08:00 · Finished: 26 Feb 2025 08:00 · Well stopped for this job: 264 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Brian Coleman, Kevin Price · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0049-0121 on 2025-02-13 Report written: 26 Feb 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that a damp, dark patch appeared along the flowline route. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0049-0121 showed the wellhead at 19.8 °C with the air at 13.2 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. Excavation found a corrosion pinhole on the bottom of the line. The well stayed shut in for about 9 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Internal corrosion from produced water collecting at a low point.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in a new section of line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joint.
  5. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: cut out and replaced the corroded flowline section.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 390 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 312 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Oily soil from the excavation and the cut-out pipe sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0049-017 (WS-06).
